parsed.version: 02024R1689-20260727 (consolidated version after the Omnibus, amending act 32026R1744)
parsed.quote: Codes of practice shall be ready at the latest by 2 May 2025.
parsed.answer: Under Article 56(9), the codes of practice for general-purpose AI models had to be ready by 2 May 2025 at the latest. The AI Office was to take the necessary steps, including inviting providers. If a code could not be finalised by 2 August 2025, or if the AI Office found it inadequate, the Commission may set common rules through implementing acts instead. In the consolidated version in force on 5 October 2026, these dates read exactly as they do in the original text.

parsed.quote: Chapter III Section 4, Chapter V, Chapter VII and Chapter XII and Article 78 shall apply from 2 August 2025, with the exception of Article 101;
parsed.answer: Article 101 applies from 2 August 2026. Article 113(b) brings Chapter XII (penalties) into application on 2 August 2025, but it expressly leaves out Article 101. raw: {"date":"2027-08-01","version":"02024R1689-20260727 (consolidated text as amended by the Omnibus, Regulation (EU) 2026/1744)","article":"Article 96(1)(g)","quote":"such guidelines shall be published by 1 August 2027.","answer":"The Commission must publish these guidelines by 1 August 2027. raw: {"date":null,"version":"02024R1689-20260727 (consolidated after Omnibus Regulation (EU) 2026/1744)","article":"Article 28(8)","quote":"shall ensure that the conformity assessment body that applies for designation both pursuant to this Regulation and the Union harmonisation legislation listed in Section A of Annex I is provided with the possibility to submit a single application and undergoes a unified assessment procedure","answer":"Yes. parsed.quote: In the case of SMEs, including start-ups, each fine referred to in this Article shall be up to the percentages or amount referred to in paragraphs 3, 4 and 5, whichever thereof is lower.
parsed.answer: No. In the consolidated text in force on 5 October 2026, the 'whichever is lower' cap in Article 99(6) still covers only SMEs, including start-ups. The Omnibus did not extend it to small mid-cap enterprises. An SMC that is not an SME therefore falls under the general rule in Article 99(4) and (5): the fine can go up to the fixed amount or the percentage of worldwide annual turnover, whichever is higher.
